heading: REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN.
translated_text:
REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Singkawang.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Singkawang City.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

6. Victim is a child and woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
7. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, the community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Special protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
10. Violence against women and children hereinafter referred to as violence is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability of women and children to enjoy all their rights and freedoms.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
15. Services are actions taken as soon as possible for the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

16. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
17. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is a regional apparatus organization within the Singkawang City Government.
18. Prevention is an activity carried out so that acts of violence against children and women do not occur.
19. Return is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to the family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
21. Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with families, communities, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
23. Agency is a regional apparatus work unit whose duties and responsibilities are to coordinate the handling of affairs in the field of organizing the protection of children and women.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated, one-stop, and networked technical service established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions, and other institutions in efforts to empower women and protect women and children comprehensively from various types of discrimination and non-violence, including human trafficking.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations, and/or community organizations.
27. Regional Action Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
28. Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Regional Government that coordinates policies, programs, and activities for the protection of children and women in the region.
29. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the Regional Government, community, and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs, and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS

heading: Article 4
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS
translated_text:
Article 4

Every victim has the right to report and receive assistance and to receive guarantees regarding their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member and as a community member.

heading: Article 5
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS
translated_text:
Article 5

The rights as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (3) letter c, are also given to the families of witnesses and/or victims up to the second degree, if the families of witnesses and/or victims receive threats both physical and psychological from other people in connection with the testimony of witnesses and/or victims.

heading: CHAPTER III
CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

The obligations and responsibilities of organizers of child and women protection are the joint responsibility of the Regional Government, community, family, and parents or guardians.

heading: Article 8
Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

{ 1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 shall be implemented in the form of community participation in the implementation of the protection of children and women.

2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur;
c. providing assistance to victims; and
d. playing an active role in efforts to increase the fulfillment of children's rights and the empowerment of women.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, community organizations, professional organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, mass media, and the business sector.
4. The role of community organizations, professional organizations, and educational institutions shall be carried out by taking necessary steps in accordance with their respective duties, functions, authorities, and competencies to assist in the implementation of the protection of children and women.
5. The participation of mass media shall be carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials related to the implementation of the protection of children and women with due regard to the best interests of the child and/or victim.
6. The role of the business sector shall be carried out through:
a. company policies with a child and women perspective;
b. products intended must be safe for children; and
c. contributing to the fulfillment of children's rights and the empowerment of women through corporate social responsibility.
7. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

The obligations and responsibilities of the family as referred to in Article 7, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

heading: Article 11
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

STATUS OF CHILDREN

Part One

Identity of Children

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. The identity of every child must be given from birth.  (2) The identity as referred to in paragraph ( 1) shall be set forth in a birth certificate.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

(3) The making of a birth certificate shall be based on a certificate from the person who witnessed and/or assisted the birth process.

4. In the case of a child whose birth process is unknown, and whose parents' whereabouts are unknown, the making of a birth certificate for such child shall be based on the statement of the person who found the child and completed with a police investigation report.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

( l) The organization of the making of birth certificates shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus Organization (OPD) that administers population administration affairs.

2. Provisions regarding procedures and requirements for making birth certificates as referred to in paragraph ( 1) shall be regulated by a Mayor Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Children Born from Mixed Marriages

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. If a mixed marriage occurs between a citizen of the Republic of Indonesia and a foreign citizen, the child born from such marriage shall have the right to obtain the citizenship of his or her father or mother in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
2. In the event of divorce from the marriage as referred to in paragraph (1), the child shall have the right to choose or based on a court decision, be in the custody of one of both parents.
3. In the event of divorce as referred to in paragraph (2), while the child is not yet able to make a choice, and his or her mother is a citizen of the Republic of Indonesia, for the best interests of the child or upon the request of his or her mother, the Regional Government shall be obliged to arrange the status of citizenship of the Republic of Indonesia for such child.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

CUSTODY

Article 15

1. In the event that parents as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) neglect their obligations, supervision measures may be taken against them or parental custody may be revoked.
2. Supervision measures against parents or revocation of custody as referred to in paragraph ( 1) shall be carried out through a court order.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

( 1) One of the parents, biological siblings or family up to the third degree, may submit an application to the court to obtain a court order regarding the revocation of parental custody or to take supervision measures if there are strong reasons for it as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (1).

2. If one of the parents, biological siblings, or family up to the third degree, cannot carry out their function, then the revocation of parental custody as referred to in paragraph (1) may also be submitted by an authorized official or other institution that has the authority to do so.
3. The court order as referred to in paragraph (1) may appoint an individual or government/community institution to become a guardian for the child concerned.
4. Individuals who carry out child care as referred to in paragraph (3) must be of the same religion as the religion professed by the child to be cared for.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUARDIANSHIP

Article 17

(1) In the event that a child is not capable of performing legal acts, while the parents or family are not known where they reside or their whereabouts, then a person or legal entity that meets the requirements may be appointed as guardian of the child concerned.

2. To become a guardian of a child as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through a court order.
3. The appointed guardian's religion must be the same as the religion professed by the child.
4. The guardian appointed as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be responsible for the child and must manage the property belonging to the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
5. Provisions regarding the requirements and procedures for appointing a guardian shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

ADOPTION OF CHILDREN

Article 18

1. Adoption of children may only be carried out for the best interests of the child, and is carried out based on customary practices and in accordance with the Laws and Regulations.
2. Adoption of children does not sever the blood relationship between the adopted child and his/her biological parents.
3. Adoption of children must be registered in the birth certificate without eliminating the child's initial identity.
4. Prospective adoptive parents must be of the same religion as the religion adhered to by the prospective adopted child.
5. Adoption of children by foreign nationals may only be carried out as a last resort in accordance with the Laws and Regulations.
6. In the event that the child's origin is not known, then the child's religion shall be adjusted to the religion of the majority of the local population.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Adoptive parents are obliged to inform their adopted child about his/her origin and biological parents.
2. Notification of origin and biological parents shall be carried out with due regard to the child's mental readiness.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

General

heading: Article 20
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Planning and Development of Information Systems for Children and Women

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

(1) Planning for the protection of children and women is implemented by providing data and information related to the protection of children and women in the region.

(2) Data and information as referred to in paragraph (1) concerns data on gender mainstreaming (PUG), data on mainstreaming of children's rights (PUHA), and evaluation of programs and data services.

(3) Data and information as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided by the Regional Apparatus Organization that administers the affairs of protection of children and women.

(4) Information data as referred to in paragraph (3) is required for planning policies and program interventions coordinated by the Agency.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Prevention and Protection

heading: Article 22
Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. Every Person and/or Institution is obliged to protect children and women from violence, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and neglect.
2. Protection by Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) by not making policies and actions that violate the rights of children and women.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Protection of Children

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Religion

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. Every child receives protection to worship according to his/her religion.
(2) Before the child can determine his/her choice, the religion adhered to by the child follows the religion of his/her parents.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. The Regional Government, community, family, parents, guardians, and social community institutions guarantee the protection of children in adhering to their religion.
(2) Protection of children in adhering to their religion as referred to in paragraph (1), includes fostering, guiding, and practicing religious teachings for children.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Health

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains an optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), is supported by community participation.
3. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
4. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be organized free of charge for families who are unable to afford it.
(5) Implementation of the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (4) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. Parents and families are obliged to be responsible for maintaining the health of children and caring for children from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out their responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), then the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill them.
3. The obligation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Every person is prohibited from performing abortion on a child still in the womb, except for reasons and procedures justified in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

The Regional Government, community, family, and parents or guardians are obliged to protect children from acts that interfere with the health and development of children.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Education

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. The Regional Government is obliged to organize basic education of at least 9 (nine) years for all children.
2. Parents are obliged to fulfill the child's right to obtain basic education of at least 9 (nine) years.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

The Regional Government, family, and parents or guardians are obliged to provide the widest possible opportunity for children to obtain education.

heading: Article 32
Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

(1) Children with disabilities are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain inclusive education and/or special education.
(2) Children who have special talents/advantages are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain special education.

3. Children who receive special protection are given opportunities to obtain their right to education.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

(1) The Regional Government is responsible for providing education costs and/or free education and/or special services for children from underprivileged families, neglected children, and children who reside in remote areas.

2. The responsibility of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) also includes encouraging the community to play an active role.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. Children in the educational unit environment must receive protection from physical violence, psychological violence, sexual crimes, and other crimes committed by educators, educational institutions, fellow students and/or other parties.
2. Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by educators, educational personnel, government officials and/or the community.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to develop a child-friendly school model.
(2) Child-friendly schools as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute a joint effort of school members to:
a. create a safe and comfortable environment for children at school;
b. develop children's participation in accordance with their age and maturity; and
c. provide opportunities for children from poor families and/or persons with disabilities to receive equal and fair treatment to obtain services and guidance at school.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to organize the maintenance and care of neglected children, both in institutions and outside institutions.
(2) The organization/implementation of the maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by institutions or the community.

3. To organize the maintenance and care of neglected children by institutions and the community, as referred to in paragraph (2), cooperation may be established with various related parties.
4. In the case of organizing maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (3), supervision is carried out by the Regional Apparatus Organization that administers affairs in the social sector in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

In the event that a child is neglected because one of the parents neglects their obligations, the institution or community as referred to in Article 37, the family, or an authorized official may submit an application to the court to determine the child as a neglected child.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

(1) The court determination as referred to in Article 39 simultaneously determines the place of shelter, maintenance and care of the neglected child concerned.

2. The institution or community authorized is obliged to provide a place as referred to in paragraph (1).
3. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and support the smooth care of children carried out by institutions or the community.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Special Protection

heading: Article 41
Article 42
Article 43
Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

Special protection for children who become refugees as referred to in Article 43 letter a is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

Special protection for child victims of riots, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict situations as referred to in Article 43 letters b through letter d is implemented through:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, housing, education, health, learning, and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

heading: Article 46
Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

Special protection for children from minority and isolated groups as referred to in Article 41 letter c is carried out through the provision of infrastructure and facilities to be able to enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and practice their own religion, and use their own language.

heading: Article 48
translated_text:
Article 48

Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or socially as referred to in Article 41 letter d shall be carried out through:  a. dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations related to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various institutions or government agencies, companies, labor unions, social community institutions, and the community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of children.

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

Special protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse as referred to in Article 41 letter e and involved in their production and distribution shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

{ 1) Special protection for children who are victims of pornography as referred to in Article 41 letter f shall be implemented through guidance, assistance, and social, physical health, and mental recovery efforts.

2. Guidance, assistance and social, physical health, and mental recovery shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
3. Every person is obliged to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing elements of pornography.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

Special protection for children with human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immune deficiency syndrome as referred to in Article 41 letter g shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, care, and rehabilitation efforts.

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

Special protection for child victims of kidnapping, sale, and trafficking of children as referred to in Article 41 letter h shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, care, and rehabilitation efforts by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 41 letter i shall be carried out through efforts:  a. dissemination and socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

heading: Article 54
Article 55
Article 56
translated_text:
Article 56

Special protection for children with special needs as referred to in Article 41 letter l shall be carried out through efforts: a. treatment of children in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of the child;
JDIH Kota Singkawang
b. fulfillment of the special needs of the child; and c. obtaining equal treatment with other children to achieve full social integration and individual development as much as possible.

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

Special protection for child victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 41 letter m shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, care, counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 58
translated_text:
Article 58

Special protection for children with deviant social behavior as referred to in Article 41 letter n shall be carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 59
translated_text:
Article 59

Special protection for children who are victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition as referred to in Article 41 letter o shall be carried out through counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 60
translated_text:
Article 60

Further provisions regarding special protection for children as referred to in Article 41 letters a through o shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 61
translated_text:
Article 61

Every child who becomes a victim as referred to in Article 41 letters d, f, h, i, and j has the right to file a claim in court in the form of the right to restitution which is the responsibility of the perpetrator of the crime in accordance with applicable provisions.

heading: Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Protection of Women

heading: Article 62
Article 63
translated_text:
Article 63

1. Every company is prohibited from recruiting child labor under age or exploiting children.
2. Companies must position female workers as work partners to grow the company.

heading: Article 64
Article 65
translated_text:
Article 65

(1) Female workers who work beyond working hours, the company is obliged to provide overtime pay in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

2. The company is obliged to protect occupational health and safety, and provide maternity leave rights to female workers.

(3) The company is prohibited from making policies that create discrimination against female workers.

4. Companies that violate the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3), may be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; and
c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Part Eight
translated_text:
Part Eight

Handling

heading: Article 66
Article 67
translated_text:
Article 67

1. Identification and receipt of complaints/reports as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter a includes:
a. ensuring readiness for complaints regarding child and women protection issues;
b. following up on information or complaints/reports received regarding child and women protection issues; and
c. identifying the type of problem, needs and handling plan.
(2) The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs is obliged to identify problems and receive complaints/reports.

heading: Article 68
translated_text:
Article 68

(1) Rescue actions as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter b are carried out if based on identification results it is known that the safety of the child or female victim of violence is threatened.

2. Actions as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by removing the child from the threatening situation and environment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection is obliged to carry out rescue actions and coordinate with the police or civil service police unit.

heading: Article 69
translated_text:
Article 69

(1) Placement of children or female victims of violence in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter c is carried out if based on identification results:
a. there is a threat to safety;
b. the child does not have a family/caregiver or guardian; and/or
c. the child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the community.
2. Placement as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for a certain period of time while the child or victim receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is deemed to have the readiness to care for and protect the child.

(3) Services provided to children and/or women while in temporary shelters include among others basic needs fulfillment services and psychosocial assistance.

4. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for social affairs is obliged to provide temporary shelters.
5. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for social affairs may cooperate with the civil service police or the police in efforts to maintain the security of children or women whose safety is threatened while in temporary shelters.

heading: Article 70
Article 71
Article 72
translated_text:
Article 72

1. Legal assistance services as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter d number 3 include: a . ensuring that children are accompanied by legal counsel; and  b. facilitating assistance to children and women victims of violence, both in the examination process in court proceedings and outside court proceedings.
2. The OPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs is obligated to provide or coordinate legal aid services with relevant agencies.

heading: Article 73
Article 74
translated_text:
Article 74

1. Handling as referred to in Articles 67 through Article 73 is implemented synergistically.
2. The implementation of handling as referred to in paragraph ( 1) is coordinated by the OPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
3. Further provisions regarding the technical implementation of handling children and women are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Part Nine
translated_text:
Part Nine

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid Services

heading: Article 75
translated_text:
Article 75

1. Law enforcement services constitute actions by law enforcement officials in implementing Laws and Regulations to handle cases of violence against children and women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of children and women victims of violence.
3. Law enforcement services are aimed at providing protection to children and women victims of violence or children in conflict with the law with a gender-responsive approach so that victims and perpetrators obtain justice and legal certainty.
4. For the implementation of law enforcement as referred to in paragraph ( 1), the Regional Government cooperates with relevant agencies and institutions to allocate resources to encourage the achievement of effectiveness and efficiency of law enforcement services for children and women victims of violence and children in conflict with the law in accordance with applicable provisions.

heading: Article 76
translated_text:
Article 76

Types of legal aid services for children and women victims of violence and children in conflict with the law include:  a . litigation legal aid; and
b. non-litigation legal aid.

heading: Part Ten
translated_text:
Part Ten

Facilitation of Juvenile Criminal Justice

heading: Article 77
Part Eleven
translated_text:
Part Eleven

Empowerment

heading: Article 78
CHAPTER X
Article 80
translated_text:
Article 80

( 1) P2TP2A is an integrated, one-stop and networked Women's Empowerment and Child Protection technical service unit established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions or other institutions.

2. P2TP2A is positioned under the coordination of the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate women's empowerment and child protection policies.

(4) P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit that functions as:
a. information center for children and women;
b. service center for children and women victims of violence; and
c. empowerment center for children and women.

heading: Article 81
translated_text:
Article 81

1. P2TP2A is established based on a Mayor's Decree.
2. P2TP2A membership consists of structural and non-structural elements from professionals, academics, community leaders and other elements as needed.
3. Further provisions regarding P2TP2A technical matters shall be regulated by Mayor's Regulation.

heading: Article 82
translated_text:
Article 82

1. In order to increase the effectiveness of supervision of the implementation of children's rights fulfillment, the Regional Government may establish a Regional Child Protection Commission or other similar institutions to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region.
2. The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission consists of 1 (one) chairperson, 1 (one) vice chairperson, and 7 (seven) members.
(3) The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission consists of elements from the Regional Government, religious leaders, community leaders, community organizations, business community, and community groups concerned with child protection.

heading: Article 83
Article 84
translated_text:
Article 84

In the event of changes to laws and regulations concerning the Regional Child Protection Commission, the regulation regarding the Regional Child Protection Commission shall be guided by laws and regulations which shall be further regulated by Mayor's Regulation.

BABXl

heading: CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY
translated_text:
CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY

Article 85

To ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination, concrete integrated efforts are needed between the Regional Government, community and business community through the development of KLA (Child-Friendly City).

heading: Article 86
Article 87
Article 88
Article 89
translated_text:
Article 89

1. To make the development of KLA effective, a KLA Task Force is established which is stipulated by Mayor's Decree.
2. The membership of the KLA Task Force may consist of the Regional Government, child representatives, business community, religious leaders, community leaders and other parties as needed.

heading: Article 90
CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 91

(I) Every child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, thoughts and others as well as being involved in decision-making processes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, regarding everything related to themselves and implemented based on awareness, understanding according to age and level of thinking maturity, as well as mutual willingness so that the Child can enjoy the results or obtain benefits from such decisions.

2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through the establishment of a Children's Forum.
3. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (2), is an organization whose members are children who become administrators of children's organizations, studios or children's activity groups and the like which are generally based on the development of talents, interests, abilities and use of leisure time.
4. The Children's Forum is directly fostered by the Regional Government and is intended to increase the capacity of children who have been active in various organizations in certain fields.

JDIH Kota Singkawang (5) In fostering the Children's Forum, the Regional Government may cooperate with professional organizations, community institutions, business entities that are child-responsive.

6. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be determined by the Mayor's Decree.

heading: Article 92
translated_text:
Article 92

1. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regional Government must pay attention to and accommodate children's opinions submitted through the Children's Forum.
2. The Regional Government may include representatives of the Children's Forum in the Regional Development Planning Deliberation.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

FUNDING AND REPORTING

Article 93

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Child and Women Protection in the region may be sourced from: a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Provincial Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
c. National Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and d. other legal and non-binding sources.
2. Funding as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, shall be based on the needs and financial capacity of the region.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
Article 95
translated_text:
Article 95

1. The Mayor is obliged to supervise the implementation of child and women protection in the region.
2. The community may supervise the implementation of child and women protection organized by the Regional Government through the mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

heading: Article 96
translated_text:
Article 96

1. OPD that organize child and women protection are obliged to report the implementation related to their duties and responsibilities in organizing child and women protection to the Mayor.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be submitted in writing, covering: a. administration;
b. finance;

c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XV

AWARDS

Article 97

1. The Regional Government may grant awards to any person and/or institution that is committed to giving full attention in organizing child and women protection.
2. Awards as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in the form of certificates and/or other forms.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for granting awards as referred to in paragraph (1), and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: CHAPTER XVI
CHAPTER XVII
CHAPTER XVIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVIII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 100

1. Institutions or bodies designated by the Mayor to carry out service duties that violate service principles may be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Perpetrators of acts of violence shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with applicable Laws.
3. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable Laws and Regulations.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: CHAPTER XIX
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 101

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 6 (six) months from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 102
translated_text:
Article 102

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Singkawang City.

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINGKAWANG CITY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

CHILD AND WOMEN PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for children and women is carried out based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must receive their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of a just and civilized humanity.

In Article 2 of Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection that the implementation of Child Protection is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia as well as the basic principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child including:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of the child;
c. the right to life, survival, and development; and
d. respect for the views of the child.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence that the elimination of domestic violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;

b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. victim protection.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection that Child Protection aims to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination, for the realization of Indonesian children who are qualified, of noble character, and prosperous.

In Article 4 of Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence that the elimination of domestic violence aims to: a. prevent all forms of domestic violence;
b. protect victims of domestic violence;
c. prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence; and
d. maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.
To realize law enforcement and the fulfillment of the basic rights of children and women, the Government of Singkawang City is obliged to provide protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as the fulfillment of civil rights and freedoms as set forth in a policy at the regional level.

The establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Child and Women Protection is an elaboration of higher laws and regulations that regulate the rights of children and women. In the Regional Regulation concerning Child and Women Protection, the norms formulated are efforts to address the problems faced in the implementation of child and women protection in Singkawang City.
The implementation of child and women protection is carried out to realize the fulfillment of the rights of children and women in accordance with human dignity and worth, and to receive protection from violence, discrimination, exploitation, and neglect for the realization of human resource development in Singkawang City that is faithful, intelligent, qualified, of noble character and prosperous.
